new_statements.translation: [p. 339, Aghul (village of Burshag), Syllable and prosody] 2. Stress is mobile; it may fall on the 1st or the 2nd syllable. If under inflection it lands on the 3rd syllable, the pretonic vowel drops: ʕaršíl 'elbow' – ʕaršlár (pl). [p. 308, note 117 to the Burshag noun section] All (oblique-stem) markers can carry stress. If the root is monosyllabic, stress always moves to the suffix; if disyllabic, it may stay on the root ('mosquito' mizmíz, Nsg – mizmíz-i, Esg) or move to the suffix with loss of the medial root vowel ('kid' mudúr, Nsg – mudr-í, Esg).

new_statements.rule_in_words: In the Burshag (Koshan) variety stress is confined to the first two syllables of the word and is not fixed: it sits on either the 1st or the 2nd syllable, lexically/morphologically determined; second-syllable stress predominates in practice (monosyllabic noun roots always stress the inflectional suffix, disyllabic roots are stressed mizmíz/mudúr and either keep that or shift to the suffix with syncope so that the stressed syllable is again the second: mudr-í, ʕaršlár). General Aghul descriptions (Alekseev & Sulejmanov 2001; Shaumjan 1941; Magometov apud Gasanova & Kaidov 2017) give 'usually 2nd syllable, initial in preverbal/negative verb forms', consistent with this.
new_statements.exceptions: Pretonic-vowel syncope when inflection would place stress on the 3rd syllable (ʕaršíl - ʕaršlár; mudúr - mudr-í); disyllabic roots vary lexically between root-final and suffix stress. Kodzasov also notes a separate 'compressed voice' prosodic correlation and pharyngealization spreading, unrelated to stress placement.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in citation and inflected noun forms of the Burshag village variety (data partly from E. Bandura's 1974 MSU expedition report, note 115). Verb accentuation is not described for Burshag; Kodzasov's parallel Richa (Keren dialect) entry adds 'neavtomaticheskoe.. v neodnoslozhnyx imenax obychno na 2-m sloge'.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes the speech of the village Burshag (Бурщаг/Буршаг), one of the three Koshan-dialect villages (Burshag, Arsug, Khudig) that constitute Glottolog's kosh1245 Qushan Aghul; Velieva 2007 names Arsug and Burshag as the dialect's core. General-Aghul stress statements (Alekseev & Sulejmanov 2001, Shaumjan 1941, Tarlanov 1994, Gasanova & Kaidov 2017) are based on Tpig/literary Aghul = aghu1253 and are not Koshan-specific. Dirr 1907 describes Burkikhan (Gequn dialect, aghu1253), explicitly not Koshan.

sources.citation: Gasanova, S. N. & Kaidov 2017. Sovremennyj agul'skij jazyk. Makhachkala. pp. 17-18 'Udarenie'.
sources.note: Literary (Tpig-based) Aghul: dynamic, mostly 2nd syllable from the beginning, movable; summarizes Magometov 1970:19-22 and Sulejmanov 1993:40-42 (preverbs stressed, negative forms initial, -di oblique suffix exception). No Koshan-specific remark.

sources.citation: Maisak, T. A. & S. R. Merdanova. 2002. [Glagol'naja sistema xpjukskogo govora agul'skogo jazyka], p. 16.
sources.note: Huppuq' dialect: stress on the 2nd syllable in all verb forms, shift in forms with prefixal negation. Notes Koshan is not mutually intelligible with other dialects. Not Koshan.

sources.citation: Tarlanov, Z. K. 1994. Aguly: ix jazyk i istorija. Petrozavodsk (archive.org scanned text).
sources.note: p. 245, general Aghul: dynamic, weak; disyllables final syllable; tri- and polysyllables gravitate to the middle; may be initial on negative prefix da- (irregular) or first member of compounds. Not Koshan-specific.

sources.note: Burshag (Koshan) village variety: mobile stress, may fall on 1st or 2nd syllable; if inflection would put it on the 3rd syllable the pretonic vowel drops (ʕaršíl 'elbow' - ʕaršlár pl). Note 117: all oblique-stem suffixes can bear stress; monosyllabic roots always shift stress to the suffix, disyllabic roots either keep it (mizmíz - mizmíz-i) or shift with syncope (mudúr - mudr-í). Sister section 15b Richa: 'podvizhnoe, neavtomaticheskoe, 1-j ili 2-j slog (v neodnoslozhnyx imenax obychno na 2-m)'.
